alex_m: Heads up — prod-rt-2 hit an OOM cascade at 15:03 UTC after yesterday's allocator soft-tuning. Not a single huge request, rather many medium requests with long prefix KV growth.

alex_m: Quick profiler snapshot (hotspots):
```
GPU mem used: 78% -> spike to 101% over ~18s
Top allocs: workspace (45%), kvcache (30%), transient kernels (18%)
Kernel selector: preferred fast-matmul path (fused) but fallback logs show switching to safe-conv in-flight often (regression since kernel-selector patch)
Batching: batch size distribution skewed — many 1-3 token requests plus occasional 512-token bursts -> batching heuristics kept large slots open and reserved workspace that never got reclaimed
Thread samples: spike aligned with large prefix expansions from long-chat user sessions (kvcache growth not evicted)
```

alex_m: Root cause hypothesis: allocator headroom reduction + new kernel-selection ranking = more transient workspace allocation and slower KV eviction; combined with batching heuristic that kept max_workspace pegged. Result: small bursts accumulate and push over cap.

tara_s: Can we flip a short-term escape hatch to buy time? Suggestions: 1) force kernel_fallback=safe for that pool 2) lower max_batch_size to 8 3) enable ephemeral_kv_clip (soft) 4) lower workspace_cap_pct from 0.75 -> 0.6

vikram_r: Agreed. Proposed immediate commands to apply (run on control plane quick window):
```bash
# lower batch size routing for prod-rt-2 pool
curl -X PATCH https://controlplane/api/v1/pools/prod-rt-2 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP' -d '{"max_batch_size":8}'

# force kernel selector to safe-mode for pool
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/pools/prod-rt-2/flags -d '{"kernel_safe_mode":true}'

# soft clip kvcache per-session entries > 2k tokens
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/runtime/config -d '{"kv_prefetch_clip":2000}'
```

vikram_r: Also can enable ephemeral spill-to-host for workspace allocations as a temporary mitigation: `evict_policy=spill-host-soft` (costly but prevents OOM).

oncall_jen: I'll approve a short maintenance window. ETA to apply changes once infra ok: 5m. Who will watch telemetry?

alex_m: I can watch traces and token-level mem charts. Tara, can you prepare a rollback plan if perf regressed?

tara_s: Rollback plan: revert three patches in order (kernel_safe_mode off, revert max_batch_size, revert kv_clip). If we see latency > 2x or throughput drop > 30%, rollback early. I'll push a canary first (10% traffic) then ramp.

alex_m: Quick gating checklist before apply:
- confirm controlplane patch idempotent
- set alert: `oom_rate>0.1%` to paging channel
- snapshot current allocations and profiles

vikram_r: Applying now to canary subset (prod-rt-2-canary). Will post status.

infra-bot: deploy-bot started patch: cp-patch-4421 by vikram_r -> target prod-rt-2-canary (flags: kernel_safe_mode=true, max_batch_size=8, kv_prefetch_clip=2000)

vikram_r: Canary applied. Initial results (2m): OOMs stopped on canary nodes, p99 latency +18%, throughput -9%. KV hit-rate dropped 6% (expected).

alex_m: Good. Next step: enable `buffer_reuse_soft_limit=0.85` globally for this pool (let reuse reclaim more aggressively). Also enable `prefetch_backoff` so long sessions don't prefetch aggressively.

vikram_r: Patching buffer_reuse and prefetch backoff.

infra-bot: deploy-bot completed patch: cp-patch-4422 -> prod-rt-2-canary

tara_s: Observing metrics for 10min window. If tail latency stabilizes and OOMs remain suppressed, ramp to 30% then 60%.

alex_m: FYI we also rolled an emergency eval to check quality impact of kernel_safe_mode on hallucination risk (small perf diff so far).

oncall_jen: Ramp to 30% started. I'll keep paging off until we confirm no regressions.

vikram_r: Ramp to 60% done. OOM alert cleared. p99 latency trending back to baseline. We'll keep kernel_safe_mode until we fix kernel selector ranking and a proper allocator headroom increase.

alex_m: Action items created: [A1] revert allocator headroom change and run controlled experiment (alex_m) [A2] audit kernel-selector patch and add fallback scoring test (vikram_r) [A3] revise batching heuristic to shrink idle slots after 200ms (tara_s) [A4] add kvcache TTL and per-session soft-eviction for long chats (platform team)

tara_s: I'll schedule a postmortem doc with timeline + perf diffs. Link will go to #postmortems.

vikram_r: noted — leaving kernel_safe_mode in place on prod-rt-2 until A2 is done and we confirm allocator tuning in A1.

alex_m: Thanks team. If anyone sees a re-occurrence, @oncall_jen please escalate immediately.

infra-bot: Incident badge assigned: INC-2026-0118. Updated incident log: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0118

vikram_r: Closing note: small config knobs (workspace_cap_pct, buffer_reuse_soft_limit, kv_clip) are effective stopgaps. We should add an automated escape-hatch runbook that applies these three in one API call for future incidents.

alex_m: Agreed — will draft a 1-pager escape-hatch playbook and attach to runbooks repo. Monitoring will remain on for 24h.

oncall_jen: 24h watch started. All good for now. :white_check_mark:
